description: H100 Fife is SGN's pioneering demonstration of a 100 percent hydrogen gas network for heating and cooking in Buckhaven and Denbeath on the Fife coast of Scotland. The network will supply up to 300 local homes with renewable hydrogen made by a dedicated electrolysis plant at Fife Energy Park powered by a nearby offshore wind turbine, designed and built to the safety and reliability standards of the existing gas system, with an on-site storage unit sized to hold enough hydrogen to keep supply during the coldest weather. Progress recorded on the page includes construction of the hydrogen network, installation of a 5 MW alkaline water electrolyser bought from Nel with six storage tanks, training of more than 70 Gas Safe registered engineers at a hydrogen training centre, the opening of Scotland's first hydrogen demonstration homes, the start of commissioning and preparation for connecting customer homes on a rolling basis. Access: the SGN page and the H100 Fife project website, free to read; the page states no licence. Caveats: a company-published project summary with no measured data or model files, and outcomes are still in progress. It suits hydrogen network conversion planning and safety case design, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
